items.stem: A manager says 'we bought a CRM, so our customer management is sorted.' What is the flaw?

options.text: CRM is a strategy and set of processes, not just a software purchase
options.rationale: Correct: without aligned processes and adoption, the software alone changes little.

options.text: Buying software always fixes customer management
options.rationale: Tools without process and adoption rarely deliver value.

options.text: CRM has nothing to do with processes
options.rationale: Process and strategy are central to CRM.
It can, through strategy, process and good data.

items.explanation: Correct: without aligned processes and adoption, the software alone changes little.

items.stem: Which practices improve the value of CRM data? (Select TWO)

options.text: Setting standards for how data is captured
options.rationale: Correct: consistent capture keeps data usable and trustworthy.
Correct: maintenance preserves data quality over time.

options.text: Collecting as much data as possible regardless of quality
Letting every user invent their own fields freely
options.rationale: Uncontrolled fields fragment and corrupt the data.

items.explanation: Correct: consistent capture keeps data usable and trustworthy.

items.stem: Reps refuse to use a new CRM and keep private spreadsheets. What should a manager address first?

options.text: Adoption: why the process and tool are not fitting users' work
options.rationale: Correct: the core issue is adoption and process fit, not the software itself.
Switching tools rarely solves an adoption problem.

options.text: Ignore it, as spreadsheets are equivalent
options.rationale: Fragmented data undermines forecasting and service.

items.explanation: Correct: the core issue is adoption and process fit, not the software itself.
